page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the Eadv6 series, executed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 AMD processor configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs. It offers a constrained-core ratio derived from the 96-core chassis, maintaining a massive memory footprint of 672.0 GB RAM, which equates to 28.0 GB of memory per allocated vCPU. The instance does not include graphical processing units.

For high-speed temporary scratch space and caching, the server includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It is also capable of attaching Premium Storage tiers. Network connectivity is unbundled from complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated allocation if public routing is needed. The combination of high local disk capacity and an expanded memory-to-core allocation targets data-heavy workloads requiring high memory bandwidth and local input-output throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained core architecture allows organizations to lower per-core database software licensing expenses while retaining the full memory capacity and high NVMe storage allocation of an enterprise-tier host. Primary workload fits include enterprise relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, large in-memory caching systems, and high-memory analytics processing where compute requirements are modest relative to data volume.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on x86_64 AMD hardware running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 24 dedicated vCPUs paired with 672.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high density of 28.0 GB of memory per core. Storage capabilities are reinforced by an integrated 5670 GB local NVMe SSD alongside support for Premium Storage, while GPU acceleration is not provided. By maintaining the memory and storage capacity of a 96-vCPU chassis while capping execution at 24 cores, this instance optimizes licensing expenditures for core-licensed database software without sacrificing memory headroom or local drive performance. It is well-suited for memory-intensive relational databases, large-scale caching engines, and enterprise data analytics pipelines requiring high I/O throughput.
